senses.definition: One of the first teeth that grow in, most often later replaced with another tooth.
senses.example: A baby tooth came loose and moved a little.

senses.definition: The part of a view or picture that seems farthest behind the main things in it.
senses.example: The artist painted snowy mountains in the background.

senses.definition: An extra copy kept in case you lose the one you use.
senses.example: The backup had my school project after the laptop stopped working.

senses.definition: A tiny living thing made of one cell. Some help other living things, while others can cause illness.
senses.example: One kind of bacterium makes food using chemicals near a deep-sea vent.

senses.definition: Long strips in some whales’ mouths that work like a strainer to catch tiny food.
senses.example: The blue whale used its baleen to hold krill while water flowed back out.

senses.definition: Small hard balls and the rings that guide them, allowing parts of a machine to roll past each other smoothly.
senses.example: The wheel used a ball bearing to turn around its axle.

senses.definition: A tank that can hold water or air to change how a boat or submarine floats.
senses.example: Water entered the ballast tank as the submarine went deeper.

senses.definition: A paper or another tool that lists choices for an election and lets a voter mark a choice.
senses.example: Ana watched her mother fill in a ballot at the voting place.

senses.definition: A drawing that uses bars of different lengths to compare amounts.
senses.example: The longest bar in our bar graph showed the class’s most popular fruit.

senses.definition: A machine-readable pattern that stands for numbers or other information.
senses.example: The shop scanner read the barcode on a juice bottle.

senses.definition: To trade goods or work directly without using money.
senses.example: The neighbors decided to barter tomatoes for a jar of jam.

senses.definition: An exchange in which people trade goods or work directly instead of paying money.
senses.example: We practiced barter by swapping paper fruit for drawings.

senses.definition: One of the places a runner tries to reach safely in a game such as baseball.
senses.example: The runner reached first base just before the ball got there.

senses.definition: Two pieces that fit together as one rung on the ladder shape of DNA.
senses.example: Each base pair connects the two sides of DNA.

senses.definition: A broad low area or the whole area where water drains toward the same place.
senses.example: Rain in the river basin eventually reaches the same river.

senses.definition: A wide bowl or a sink that can hold water.
senses.example: We filled the basin with warm water to wash the mud from our hands.

senses.definition: A flying mammal with wings made of thin skin stretched over long finger bones.
senses.example: A bat flew over the pond hunting insects.

senses.definition: A club used to hit a ball in a game such as baseball or cricket.
senses.example: I picked up the bat when it was my turn to hit.

senses.definition: To hit, or try to hit, a ball with a bat.
senses.example: Each player will bat once in this practice.

senses.definition: A short stick carried and passed in a relay, or a short stick a conductor uses to guide musicians.
senses.example: The runner took the baton without slowing down.

senses.definition: A device that uses stored chemical energy to push electric charge around a circuit.
senses.example: A battery lets the flashlight work without plugging it into a wall.

senses.definition: A regular pulse you can often tap along with in music.
senses.example: We marched to the beat of the drum.

senses.definition: A muscle at the front of your upper arm that helps bend your elbow.
senses.example: Your biceps muscle works when you bend your elbow to lift a bag.

senses.definition: A liquid made by the liver that helps the body digest fats.
senses.example: Bile helps spread fat into small droplets.

senses.definition: A plan for a new law, written so lawmakers can talk about it and vote on it.
senses.example: The state lawmakers discussed a bill about public libraries.

senses.definition: Using only two choices, like the digits 0 and 1 in computer numbers.
senses.example: In binary counting, 10 means two.

senses.definition: A way to look in a sorted list by checking the middle and deciding which half to keep looking in.
senses.example: The program uses binary search to find a number in a sorted row.

senses.definition: Light made by a living thing using a process inside its body.
senses.example: A deep-sea fish can use bioluminescence to shine in the dark.

senses.definition: A small piece or amount of something.
senses.example: There was a bit of icing left on the spoon.

senses.definition: A tiny unit of computer information that can be 0 or 1.
senses.example: Three bits can store one of eight different patterns.

senses.definition: A stretchy pouch inside the body that holds urine until you pee.
senses.example: The bladder gets larger as it fills with urine.

senses.definition: A tube inside an animal that carries blood.
senses.example: Blood moving through a blood vessel brings supplies to cells.

senses.definition: A thick layer of fat under the skin that helps keep some ocean mammals warm.
senses.example: A seal has blubber between its skin and muscles.

senses.definition: An area of land that stays very wet, where partly decayed plants build up in the ground.
senses.example: Some kinds of moss can grow in a bog.

senses.definition: The temperature at which a liquid starts boiling at a particular pressure.
senses.example: The boiling point of water is lower on a high mountain.

senses.definition: Soft tissue inside certain bones. One kind makes new blood cells.
senses.example: The red bone marrow in some bones makes blood cells.

senses.definition: Having to do with the two values true and false, or rules that use those values.
senses.example: A Boolean question could ask whether the light is on.

senses.definition: A line that shows where one area ends and another begins.
senses.example: The old stone wall marks the boundary between the two yards.

senses.definition: A limit that makes clear what is allowed or welcome.
senses.example: Asking people to knock before entering my room is a boundary.

senses.definition: A long tool strung with hair or another fiber, drawn across strings to play a violin or a related instrument.
senses.example: The violinist drew the bow across the lowest string.

senses.definition: An organized refusal to buy, use, or take part in something in order to protest.
senses.example: The boycott lasted more than a year as residents refused to ride the buses.

senses.definition: A little salty, as water can be where a river mixes with the sea.
senses.example: The marsh creek held brackish water when the tide came in.

senses.definition: A way to read and write using patterns of raised dots that can be felt with the fingers.
senses.example: A sign with braille let the visitor check the room number by touch.

senses.definition: The organ inside your head that takes in signals and helps control the body.
senses.example: Your brain helps you remember what you learned yesterday.

senses.definition: The outer layers of a grain that may be taken off when it is milled.
senses.example: Brown rice still has bran around its lighter center.

senses.definition: An instrument played by buzzing into a mouthpiece, such as a trumpet or trombone.
senses.example: A trumpet player makes a brass instrument sound by buzzing their lips.

senses.definition: To help people feel more comfortable and start talking when they first meet or feel shy.
senses.example: The teacher asked everyone to share a favorite snack to break the ice.

senses.definition: To carry or guide someone or something to a place or to another person.
senses.example: Please bring your library book to school tomorrow.

senses.definition: An app that requests and shows web pages.
senses.example: I opened a library website in my browser.

senses.definition: An error in software or computer equipment that makes it work differently from how it should.
senses.example: A bug made the game jump back to the start.

senses.definition: A short plant stem with thick layers that store food, often found underground.
senses.example: A tulip bulb can grow a fresh shoot in spring.

senses.definition: The upward push that a liquid or gas gives to something in it.
senses.example: The buoyancy of the water helped hold the boat up.

senses.definition: An underground passage or home made or used by an animal.
senses.example: The meerkat ran into its burrow when another meerkat called.

senses.definition: To get something by paying money for it.
senses.example: We saved enough to buy a new soccer ball.

senses.definition: A group of eight bits that a computer handles as a unit.
senses.example: A file with 100 bytes contains 800 bits.
